query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The substitution of a fraction of Fe in FeCoNi with Cr will produce a high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives.
generation.intervention: Substitution of a fraction of Fe with Cr
generation.conditions: The resulting alloy should have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a mixed structure of fcc and bcc phases, with the bcc phase having a higher coercivity
generation.mechanism: The substitution of Cr for Fe will lead to a change in the magnetic properties of the alloy, resulting in a higher coercivity due to the increased magnetic anisotropy
generation.predicted_outcome: The resulting FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy will have a higher coercivity than the prior derivatives, such as FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt.
generation.baseline: The coercivity of the prior derivatives, such as FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt.
generation.boundary: The substitution of Cr for Fe should be done in a way that maintains the high-entropy alloy characteristics, such as an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Cr substitution required to achieve the desired coercivity is uncertain and may need to be determined experimentally.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with varying amounts of Cr substitution, and measure their coercivity and microstructure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercivity of the resulting alloys does not increase with Cr substitution, or if the microstructure does not show a mixed structure of fcc and bcc phases, then the hypothesis is falsified.

Influence of Cr Substitution and Temperature on Hierarchical Phase Decomposition in the AlCoFeNi High Entropy Alloy

Abstract: While the AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy exhibits a single ordered B2 phase at high temperature, both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution. The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy. The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions. Additionally, it is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity. The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys.

Magnetic Properties and Microstructure of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) High-Entropy Alloys

Abstract: The present work exhibits the effects of Sn addition on the magnetic properties and microstructure of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The results show all the samples consist of a mixed structure of face-centered-cubic (FCC) phase and body-centered-cubic (BCC) phase. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nano-precipitates in BCC matrix. It also shows that the Curie temperatures (Tc) of the FCC phase and the saturation magnetization (Ms) of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs increase greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases after the addition of Sn into FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA. The thermomagnetic curves indicate that the phases of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs will transform from FCC with low Tc to BCC phase with high Tc at temperature of 600–700 K. This work provides a new idea for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs for their potential application as soft magnets to be used at high temperatures.
